paragraphs: Savers Value Village, Inc. (the "Company", "we", "us", or "our") is the largest for-profit thrift operator in the United States ("U.S.") and Canada based on number of stores. With nearly 24,000 team members, we operate a total of 367 stores under the Savers®, Value Village®, Value Village Boutique™, Village des ValeursMD, Unique® and 2nd Ave.® banners. As of January 3, 2026, we had 179 stores in the U.S., 170 stores in Canada and 18 stores in Australia.

The Company reports on a fiscal year basis, which ends on the Saturday nearest December 31. Our last three fiscal years consisted of the 53 weeks ended January 3, 2026 ("fiscal 2025"), the 52 weeks ended December 28, 2024 ("fiscal 2024") and the 52 weeks ended December 30, 2023 ("fiscal 2023").
Our mission is to champion reuse and inspire a future where secondhand is second nature.
From the thrill of the hunt to the joy of decluttering, we help communities harness the power of pre-loved stuff to keep reusable items around for years to come.

We are committed to redefining secondhand shopping by providing one-of-a-kind, low-priced merchandise ranging from quality clothing to home goods in an exciting treasure-hunt shopping environment. We purchase secondhand textiles (e.g., clothing, bedding and bath items), shoes, accessories, housewares, books and other goods from our non-profit partners ("NPPs"). We then process, select, price, merchandise and sell these items in our stores. Items that are unsuited for or unsold at retail stores are marketed to wholesale customers who reuse or repurpose the items they purchase from us. We believe our hyper-local and socially responsible procurement model, industry-leading and innovative operations, differentiated value proposition and deep relationships with our customers distinguish us from other secondhand and value-based retailers. Our business model is rooted in sustainability and contributing to the communities we serve, with a mission to positively impact our stakeholders: thrifters, NPPs and their donors, our team members and our stockholders. As a leader and pioneer of the for-profit thrift category, we seek to positively impact the environment by reducing waste and extending the life of reusable goods. The vast majority of the clothing and textiles we source is sold to our retail or wholesale customers.

We offer a dynamic, ever-changing selection of items, with an average unit retail price ("AUR") of approximately $5. We have a highly engaged customer base, with over 6.1 million active loyalty program members in the U.S. and Canada who shopped with us during fiscal 2025, driving 72.7% of retail sales for the year.

We have innovated and invested in the development of significant operational expertise in order to integrate the three highly complex parts of thrift operations—supply and processing, retail and sales to wholesale markets. Our business model enables us to provide value to our NPPs and our customers, while driving attractive profitability and cash flow.

Our strategy is to locally source our merchandise by purchasing secondhand items donated to our NPPs, which provides them with revenue to support their community-focused missions. This also aids in creating a broad and diverse selection for our customers, fosters a sense of community, and reduces transportation costs and emissions typically associated with the production and distribution of new merchandise. While purchases made by our customers in our stores do not directly benefit any NPP, we pay a market-competitive contractual rate to purchase donated items.

We source our merchandise primarily through three distinct and strategic procurement models: (i) on-site donations ("OSDs"), (ii) GreenDrop locations and (iii) delivered supply. Increasing the proportion of OSDs and GreenDrop as a percentage of total supply is desirable, as donations from these sources are generally of higher quality and collectively have a contractually lower cost than product sourced through other channels, which benefits sales yield, and ultimately, our gross product margin. OSDs and GreenDrop are collectively the largest part of our supply mix and accounted for 78.0% and 76.3% of total pounds processed for fiscal 2025 and 2024, respectively.

•OSDs: Donations of items by individuals to our NPPs, made at Community Donation Centers ("CDCs") located at our stores. We operate as a registered professional fundraiser where required, accepting donations on behalf of our NPPs. Each store is specifically designated as an OSD location for a particular NPP, such that all donations received at the CDC are credited to that NPP.

•GreenDrop locations: Attended donation stations that collect donations of items made by individuals to our NPPs at well-signed brick and mortar or trailer locations conveniently located closer to attractive donor neighborhoods in the same market as a store. On behalf of our NPPs, we solicit, collect and deliver items from our GreenDrop locations to our stores and Centralized Processing Centers ("CPCs").

•Delivered supply: Delivered supply comprises donations delivered either to our CPCs or directly to our stores. This channel supplements OSDs and GreenDrop collections by addressing remaining assortment and volume needs necessary to offer customers a full and balanced product mix. Donations may be collected by our NPPs through neighborhood collections, donation drives, or similar methods, or we may solicit, collect and deliver items on behalf of our NPPs.

•Donation drives: Donation drives operate within our FUNDrive® program and include smaller, local non-profits such as schools, sports teams, community groups and other charitable organizations. These drives are one-time and event-based, with contractual agreements based on each distinct donation drive itself.

•Third-party credential: Third-party credential goods are purchased in small amounts on an as-needed basis from regional for-profit collectors, generally consisting of bin operators and other for-profit resellers.

Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry
If we fail to obtain a sufficient quantity of new and recurring quality secondhand items at attractive prices, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be harmed.
We are subject to various risks to our physical store and processing facility locations, including with respect to the sourcing, processing, storage and other logistics of secondhand items.

Our business depends on our ability to attract and retain suitable workers for our stores and processing facilities and to manage labor costs, particularly given recent disruptions in the supply and cost of labor.
Both supply of and demand for our products is influenced by general economic conditions, including trends in consumer spending.
If we fail to manage our growth effectively and execute our business plan, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be harmed.
We lease virtually all of our locations and must identify, obtain and retain suitable locations for our stores and processing facilities to achieve our planned growth.

Our continued growth depends on attracting new, and retaining existing, customers, including by increasing the acceptance of thrift among new and growing customer demographics, and effective advertising.
We have significant foreign operations, particularly in Canada, that subject us to additional operating risks and certain exchange rate risks, which we may not be able to fully hedge.
Natural disasters, pandemics, geo-political events and other highly disruptive events can have an unpredictable and adverse impact on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
If we are unable to successfully leverage technology to automate and drive efficiencies, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be harmed.
Labor-related matters, including labor disputes, may adversely affect our operations.
Disruptions in the wholesale markets due to market conditions, conditions in the countries where our wholesale goods are sold or other factors may adversely affect our business.

We may not succeed in promoting and maintaining our reputation, and our business could be negatively impacted by a failure, or perceived failure, to live up to our sustainability and corporate citizenship commitments.
Risks Relating to Information Technology, Intellectual Property, Data Security and Privacy
Compromises of our data security, including cyberattacks or data breaches, could cause us to incur unexpected expenses and may materially harm our reputation and results of operations.
Our use of artificial intelligence tools and changes to related laws or regulations could adversely affect our business.
We may be unable to protect our intellectual property rights, and we may be accused of infringing on the intellectual property or other proprietary rights of third parties.

We rely on software, technology and services from other parties. Defects in or the loss of access to software or services from third parties could increase our costs and adversely affect the quality of our products.
paragraphs: Below is a summary of the principal factors that we believe make an investment in the Company speculative or risky. This summary does not address all of the risks that we face. Additional discussion of the risks summarized in this risk factor summary, and other risks that we face, can be found after this summary, and should be carefully considered, together with other information in this Annual Report and our other filings with the SEC, before making an investment decision.
•The success of our business model depends on our ability to source quality secondhand items at attractive prices.

•The sourcing and other logistics of processing secondhand items, especially from local communities, can be subject to fluctuating costs and can have other risks that could negatively impact our business.
•Our growth and performance depend on the efforts of our store and processing center team members and may be negatively affected by the labor market and employee relations.

•Our extensive operations domestically and internationally are subject to global economic conditions, require us to manage different retail and wholesale environments and subject us to exchange rate risks.

•Our ability to grow may be negatively affected by perceptions of thrift, trends in consumer discretionary spending, our operational ability to manage growth and the availability of new store locations.

paragraphs: Savers Value Village, Inc. (the "Company", "we", "us", or "our") 為美國 ("U.S.") 與加拿大根據商店數量而言最大的營利性 thrift 操作商 ("thrift operator")。擁有近 24,000 名員工，我們在 Savers®, Value Village®, Value Village Boutique™, Village des ValeursMD, Unique® 和 2nd Ave.® 燈號下經營總計 367 家商店。截至 2026 年 1 月 3 日，我們在美國有 179 家商店，在加拿大有 170 家商店，在澳洲有 18 家商店。
本公司以財務年度為基礎進行財務報導，財務年度結算日為 12 月 31 日最近的星期六。我們最近三個財務年度分別為 2025 財年（截至 2026 年 1 月 3 日的 53 週）、2024 財年（截至 2024 年 12 月 28 日的 52 週）以及 2023 財年（截至 2023 年 12 月 30 日的 52 週）。
我們的使命是倡導重複使用，並啟發一個第二手商品成為日常習慣的未來。
從尋寶的興奮到整理物品的喜悅，我們協助社區善用二手商品的潛力，讓可重複使用的物品持續使用多年。

我們致力於重新定義二手購物，透過提供獨一無二、價格低廉的商品，從高品質服飾到居家用品，創造一個令人興奮的尋寶式購物環境。我們從非營利機構 ("NPPs") 購買二手織物（例如服飾、牀品及浴室用品）、鞋子、配件、家用品、書籍及其他商品。我們隨後會進行處理、挑選、定價、商品化並在商店銷售這些商品。無法在零售商店銷售或不適合銷售的商品，則會行銷給重複使用或再利用所購商品的批發客戶。我們相信我們的極端在地化與社會責任採購模式、行業領先且創新運作、獨特的價值主張以及與客戶的深厚關係，使我們與其他二手及價值導向零售商有所區別。我們的商業模式根植於可持續性與對服務社區的貢獻，並以影響我們的利害關係人（包括 thrifters、NPPs 及其捐贈者、我們的員工與股東）為使命。作為營利性 thrift 分類的領導者與先驅者，我們致力於透過減少浪費與延長可重複使用商品的壽命，來正面影響環境。我們所採購的服飾與織物中，絕大多數會銷售給我們的零售或批發客戶。
我們提供一個動態且不斷變化的商品選擇，平均零售單價 ("AUR") 約為 5 美元。我們擁有高度參與的客戶羣，美國與加拿大有超過 610 萬名活躍忠誠會員，在 2025 財年有在本公司的商店購物，帶動該年度零售銷售的 72.7%。
我們已創新並投資於發展重要的運營專業知識，以整合 thrift 操作的三個高度複雜部分—供應鏈與處理、零售與向批發市場銷售。我們的商業模式使我們能為 NPPs 與客戶提供價值，同時驅動有吸引力的獲利與現金流。
我們的策略是透過從 NPPs 購買捐贈的二手商品來本地採購商品，這為 NPPs 提供收入以支持其社區導向的使命。這也協助我們為客戶提供廣泛且多樣的商品選擇，促進社區感，並減少與生產與分銷新商品通常相關的運輸成本與排放。雖然我們商店中客戶的購買並不會直接利益任何 NPP，我們會以市場競爭性的合約價格購買捐贈物品。

我們主要透過三種不同且戰略性的採購模式來取得商品：(i) 現場捐贈（"OSDs"），(ii) GreenDrop 站點以及 (iii) 送達供應。提高 OSDs 與 GreenDrop 在總供應量中所佔的百分比是有利的，因為這些來源的捐贈品通常品質較高，且集體而言成本較低，這有助於銷售收益，並最終提高我們的毛利率。OSDs 與 GreenDrop 總計為我們供應鏈中佔比最大的部分，於財務年度 2025 年及 2024 年分別佔總處理磅數的 78.0% 與 76.3%。
•OSDs：個人將物品捐贈給我們的 NPPs，並在我們商店內的社區捐贈中心（"CDCs"）進行捐贈。我們在必要時以註冊專業募款機構的身份運作，代表我們的 NPPs 接受捐贈。每家商店會被特別指定為某個 NPP 的 OSD 站點，使得在 CDC 收到的所有捐贈都計入該 NPP。
•GreenDrop 站點：這些為人所知的捐贈站點會收集個人捐贈給我們 NPPs 的物品，設置在靠近吸引捐贈者的社區，且與商店位於相同市場的實體或拖車站點。我們代表 NPPs 從 GreenDrop 站點徵集、收集並運送物品至商店及集中處理中心（"CPCs"）。
•送達供應：送達供應包含捐贈品直接送達我們的 CPCs 或商店。此渠道透過補足 OSDs 與 GreenDrop 收集的品項種類與數量需求，來提供顧客完整的產品組合。捐贈品可能由 NPPs 透過社區收集、捐贈活動或其他方法進行收集，或由我們代表 NPPs 徵集、收集並運送物品。
•捐贈活動：捐贈活動運作於我們的 FUNDrive® 程式中，包含較小規模的本地非營利組織，例如學校、運動隊伍、社區團體及其他慈善機構。這些活動為一時性且基於活動的，與每個獨特捐贈活動本身簽訂契約。
•第三方憑證：第三方憑證商品是以小批量按需從區域營利性收購者購入，通常為箱裝運營商及其他營利性販售者。

除非文意另有明確要求，本節所有提及"Savers Value Village"、"本公司"、"我們"、"我們"或"我們"的參考，均指Savers Value Village, Inc.的業務。
本討論包含涉及風險與不確定性的展望性陳述，反映我們的計畫、預估與信念。我們實際結果與特定事件的時間點可能與這些展望性陳述中預期的有顯著差異，原因包括但不限於於第一部分第1A項"風險因素"或本年度報告其他部分所列的各項因素。

我們是美國（"美國"）與加拿大根據商店數量最大的營利型 thrift 操作商（"thrift"意指二手商店），截至2026年1月3日，我們在Savers®、Value Village®、Value Village Boutique™、Village des ValeursMD、Unique®與2nd Ave.®旗號下經營總計367間商店。我們致力於重新定義二手購物，透過提供獨一無二、價格低廉的商品，從高品質服飾到居家用品，營造一個令人興奮的尋寶式購物環境。我們從非營利夥伴（"NPPs"）處購入二手織物（例如服飾、牀品與浴室用品）、鞋子、配件、家用品、書籍及其他商品。我們隨後會進行處理、選購、定價、商品化並在商店內銷售這些商品。無法適應零售商店或未在零售商店售出的商品，則會行銷給 Wholesale 客戶，這些客戶會重複使用或重新利用從我們處購入的商品。我們相信我們的極度在地化與社會責任採購模式、行業領先且創新運作、獨特的價值主張與與客戶的深厚關係，使我們與其他二手與價值導向零售商有所區別。我們的商業模式根植於永續性與對所服務社區的貢獻，並以對利害關係人（包括 thrifters、NPPs 及其捐贈者、我們的團隊成員與股東）產生正面影響為使命。作為營利型 thrift 分類的領導者與先驅者，我們致力於透過減少浪費與延長可重複使用商品的壽命，對環境產生正面影響。我們所採購的服飾與織物中，絕大多數會銷售給我們的零售或 Wholesale 客戶。

我們提供一個動態且不斷變化的商品選擇，平均零售單價（"AUR"）約為5美元。我們最積極參與的客戶為我們 Super Savers Club® 忠誠會員計畫的會員。截至2026年1月3日，我們在美國與加拿大忠誠會員計畫中總計有6.1百萬名活躍會員，在會計2025期間購物，相較於2024年12月28日的5.9百萬名總計活躍會員。活躍會員在會計2025期間帶動了72.7%的零售銷售，相較於會計2024期間的72.4%。
我們已創新並投資於發展重要的運營專業知識，以整合 thrift 運作的三個高度複雜部分—供應鏈與處理、零售與向 Wholesale 市場銷售。我們的商業模式使我們能為 NPPs 與客戶提供價值，同時驅動有吸引力的獲利與現金流。
我們的策略是透過從 NPPs 購買捐贈的二手商品，來進行本地採購，這為 NPPs 提供收入以支持其社區導向的使命。這也幫助我們為客戶提供廣泛且多樣的商品選擇，促進社區感，並減少與新商品生產與分銷通常相關的運輸成本與排放。雖然我們商店內客戶的購物行為並不會直接對任何 NPP 產生好處，我們會以市場競爭的契約價格購買捐贈物品。

我們主要透過三個區別且戰略性的採購模式來取得商品：(i) 現場捐贈（"OSDs"），(ii) GreenDrop 站點以及 (iii) 送達供應。提高 OSDs 與 GreenDrop 在總供應中所佔的百分比是有利的，因為這些來源的捐贈品通常品質較高，且集體而言成本較低，這有助於銷售產出，並最終提高我們的毛利率。OSDs 與 GreenDrop 合計為我們供應組成的最大部分，於財務年度 2025 年及 2024 年，分別佔我們總處理磅數的 78.0% 與 76.3%。
•OSDs：個人將物品捐贈給我們的 NPPs，並在我們商店內的社區捐贈中心（"CDCs"）進行捐贈。我們在必要時以註冊專業募款機構的身份運作，代表我們的 NPPs 接受捐贈。每家商店會被特別指定為某個 NPP 的 OSD 站點，因此在 CDC 收到的所有捐贈都會記入該 NPP。
•GreenDrop 站點：由個人捐贈物品至我們的 NPPs 的捐贈站點，設置在靠近吸引捐贈者社區的實體店面或拖車場地，且位於與商店相同市場的附近。我們代表 NPPs 向這些 GreenDrop 站點徵集、收集並將物品送至我們的商店與集中處理中心（"CPCs"）。
•送達供應：送達供應包含捐贈品直接送至我們的 CPCs 或商店。此渠道透過補足 OSDs 與 GreenDrop 收集，以解決剩餘的商品種類與數量需求，使我們能為客戶提供完整且平衡的商品組合。捐贈品可能由 NPPs 透過社區收集、捐贈活動或其他類似方式進行收集，或由我們代表 NPPs 徵集、收集並送達。
我們運用分析平台來衡量我們商店中每種供應來源的銷售產出與商品毛利率。通常，此工具用來定期確認現有供應來源的表現，或評估新供應來源的表現。
我們的商業模式建立在於為我們的社區客戶提供高品質的二手商品。我們能因應客戶需求，歸功於與廣泛的 NPP 網路所建立的深厚關係，這在回收業界是獨一無二的。

與我們業務及產業相關的風險
若我們無法以具吸引力的價格取得足夠數量的新品及持續性二手商品，將可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成損害。
我們的實體門市及處理設施位置面臨各種風險，包括二手商品的來源、處理、儲存及其他物流相關事項。
我們的業務取決於我們能否吸引並留住合適的員工於門市及處理設施，並有效管理勞動成本，特別是在近期勞動供應與成本出現幹擾的情況下。
我們產品的供應與需求均受總體經濟條件影響，包括消費者支出趨勢。
若我們無法有效管理成長並執行業務計畫，將可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成損害。
我們幾乎所有營運據點均為租賃，必須識別、取得並留住合適的門市及處理設施據點，以實現我們預期的成長。
我們的持續成長取決於吸引新客戶及留住現有客戶，包括增加年輕及成長中客羣對 thrift 的接受度，以及有效的廣告宣傳。
我們在加拿大等國家有重大海外營運，這使我們面臨額外的營運風險及某些匯率風險，我們可能無法完全對衝這些風險。
天然災害、疫情、地緣政治事件及其他高度幹擾性的事件，可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生無法預測且不利的影響。
若我們無法成功運用科技來自動化並提升效率，將可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況造成損害。
與勞工相關的議題，包括勞資爭議，可能對我們的營運產生不利影響。
因市場狀況、我們 Wholesale 商品銷售國家的情況或其他因素導致 Wholesale 市場中斷，可能對我們的業務產生不利影響。
我們可能無法成功推廣並維持我們的聲譽，若我們未能履行或被認為未能履行永續發展及企業公民承諾，將可能對我們的業務產生負面影響。
與資訊科技、智慧財產權、資料安全及隱私權相關的風險
我們資料安全遭侵害，包括網路攻擊或資料外洩，可能導致我們產生意外支出，並對我們的聲譽及營運結果造成重大損害。
本公司使用人工智慧工具及相關法律法規之變更可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司可能無法保護智慧財產權，且可能被指控侵權或違反第三方之專有權利。
本公司依賴其他當事人所提供之軟體、技術及服務。若軟體或服務出現瑕疵或無法取得，將增加本公司成本並對本公司產品品質產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 以下為我們認為投資本公司具有投機性或風險的主要因素摘要。此摘要並未涵蓋我們所面臨的所有風險。有關本風險因素摘要中所提及的風險，以及其他我們所面臨的風險之進一步討論，請參閱本摘要之後的內容，並應與本年度報告及其他向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）所提交之文件一併審慎考量，以作為投資決策之參考。
•我們商業模式的成功取決於我們能否以具吸引力的價格取得高品質的二手商品。
•處理二手商品之採購及其他物流，特別是來自當地社區的二手商品，可能面臨成本波動及其他風險，這些風險可能對我們的業務造成負面影響。
•我們的成長與表現取決於我們門市與處理中心團隊成員的努力，可能因勞動市場與員工關係而受到負面影響。
•我們廣泛的國內外營運業務面臨全球總體經濟條件的影響，需要我們管理不同的零售與批發環境，並使我們面臨匯率風險。
•我們成長的能力可能因節儉消費的觀念、消費者可支配支出的趨勢、我們操作能力管理成長的表現，以及新門市位置的可取得性而受到負面影響。
